resolutions.recommendation: No change to LengthKnown (2623 km). The length_ratio flag (drawn route 1,228 km geodesic vs sheet 2,623 km, ratio 0.47) is a false positive from segment-vs-network granularity, not a wrong value or a RouteAccuracy problem. Independently verified: Petronas Gas Berhad's own corporate site states the PGU pipeline network it operates is '2,623-km' / '2,623 km' (https://www.petronas.com/pgb/our-business/gas-transportation) -- an exact match to the sheet value, from the asset's operator (primary source). GEM's routes-repo geometry (P1065.geojson, 25-part MultiLineString) traces a single corridor end-to-end from ~1.46N (Johor) to ~6.45N (Perlis border) at 1,227.7 km geodesic -- i.e. it IS the full-length mainline corridor, not a partial/truncated trace, but it is only the MAINLINE. Independent trade-press documentation (Oil & Gas Journal, 'Malaysia's Peninsular Gas system gets another segment') confirms PGU is built as mainline + parallel LOOP lines + LATERAL spurs, not one single pipe: Stage III alone is described as 448 km of 36-in mainline (Meru-Pauh) split into a 184 km Meru-Lumut sector (Sector 1) PLUS a 17 km 24-in lateral to Segari power station, and a 264 km Lumut-Pauh sector (Sectors 2-3) PLUS a 3 km lateral to the Gurun fertiliser plant and optional 21 km (Prai) and 25 km (Teknologi Tenaga Perlis) laterals. Separately, PGU 'Loop 2' is documented (Saipem/trade coverage) as a 230-km 36-in pipeline from Segamat to Meru laid PARALLEL to the existing mainline (i.e. adds pipe-km with zero new map extent) plus a 40-km upgrade of existing pipe; a 'Loop 1' (Kertih-Segamat) is referenced the same way. None of these loops or laterals are separately drawn in the routes-repo geometry for P1065. Summing a single-corridor mainline of ~1,200-1,300 km against a network that layers a second parallel trunk (Loop 1 + Loop 2) and half a dozen named lateral spurs (Lumut, Segari, Gurun, Prai, Teknologi Tenaga Perlis, plus Melaka/Port Dickson/Port Klang/Johor Bahru/Georgetown per the flag's own list) comfortably closes a ~1,400 km gap. Recommendation: stage a LengthKnown [ref] citing the Petronas Gas Berhad page (fill below); do NOT touch LengthKnown, LengthKnownUnits, or RouteAccuracy. If a researcher wants a tighter accounting than 'network total, corroborated', that requires digitizing the loop lines and laterals as additional routes-repo geometry (out of scope for this QC leg) -- but the flag itself is resolved as a non-issue.
resolutions.researcher_notes: Evidence trail: (1) Computed the drawn geometry myself: `../GOIT-GGIT-pipeline-routes/data/individual-routes/gas-pipelines/P1065.geojson` is a FeatureCollection of 25 MultiLineString parts spanning lon 100.15-103.84, lat 1.46-6.45 (i.e. Johor in the south to the Perlis/Thai border in the north -- the full peninsula, not a partial trace); summed geodesic length = 1,227.7 km, matching the flag's 1,228 km. This confirms the geometry is a genuine end-to-end mainline trace, so the gap isn't a truncated/incomplete digitization. (2) Petronas Gas Berhad's own official site (operator of PGU, a primary/regulatory-equivalent source per confidence_tiers.md) states verbatim: 'the 2,623km Peninsular Gas Utilisation (PGU) pipeline network' -- https://www.petronas.com/pgb/our-business/gas-transportation (verified: HTTP 200, contains '2,623' and 'Peninsular Gas Utilisation'). This is an EXACT match to the sheet's existing LengthKnown=2623, from the entity that built and runs the asset -- sufficient alone for high tier per the rubric ('one primary/regulatory source'). (3) A second passage, from The Edge Malaysia ('Liberalising Natural Gas Market: Peninsular Malaysia's Journey', URL path content/advertise/... -- flagging this looks like sponsored/native content, likely PETRONAS-authored, so I am NOT treating it as a genuinely independent second source, just corroborating restatement), separately says 'the PGU boasts an impressive 2,623-kilometre high-pressure transmission pipeline network' and distinguishes it from the downstream 2,465-km NGDS distribution network -- useful for confirming PGU-vs-NGDS scope isn't the confusion, but not counted toward the 2-independent bar. (4) Oil & Gas Journal ('Malaysia's Peninsular Gas system gets another segment', verified HTTP 200) is genuinely independent trade press and gives concrete segment/lateral lengths for PGU Stage III (448 km mainline in two sub-sectors of 184 km and 264 km, plus 17 km, 3 km, and two ~21-25 km optional laterals) -- this doesn't restate the 2,623 km total but corroborates the STRUCTURE (mainline + laterals, built in stages) that explains why a single-corridor trace undercounts the network. (5) Wikipedia's 'Peninsula Gas Utilisation' article corroborates PGU was built in 3 phases (1984-2001) with laterals to Lumut and Gurun under Phase III, but is internally inconsistent (states both 2,623 km and, elsewhere, '2,500 kilometers') and cites a 1997 conference paper I could not independently retrieve -- used only for background, not cited as a ref. (6) Petronas' own Petrosains (science-outreach arm) posted a Facebook video captioned 'PETRONAS runs a 2623km Peninsular Gas Utilisation (PGU) gas pipeline network' -- same corporate origin as (2), not counted as independent, and Facebook is a poor ref format regardless. Could NOT establish: a published per-loop/per-lateral length breakdown that arithmetically reconciles 1,228 (mainline) + loops + laterals = 2,623 to the km -- the pieces I found (Loop 2 = 230 km + 40 km upgrade; Stage III laterals totaling roughly 40-65 km) are consistent with, but don't fully prove, the exact 2,623 figure. Given the operator's own primary-source statement matches the sheet exactly, and the network is independently documented to include a second parallel loop trunk plus multiple named laterals not drawn in the current geometry, I'm confident this is a segment(mainline)-vs-network flag, not a data error -- but a full km-by-km reconciliation of loops+laterals would need someone to digitize that geometry, which is beyond this QC leg. For the record only (deep-sweep leg already flagged, not researched here per instructions): StartYear1=1993 doesn't match any phase-completion date I saw (1984/1992/1998/2001 all appear instead); Owner1 'Petronas 100%' is likely more precisely Petronas Gas Berhad, PGB's own pages describe it as the network operator and PGB is a separately-listed, not-wholly-Petronas-owned subsidiary.

resolutions.recommendation: No change to LengthKnownKm (662) — it is the officially reported project length and is now backed by three independent verified refs. This is a route-drawing problem, not a spec problem: the drawn geometry is a single 380 km LineString running roughly straight Kimanis (6.128N, 116.147E) to Tawau (4.405N, 117.919E), but every independent description of the project routes it via Sandakan (and Lahad Datu) on the east coast, not point-to-point. A GulfPub PE World Map scrape of the same project (Tier-2, not citable, but useful for shape) splits it into two segments — Kimanis to Sandakan (270.37 km / 267.08 km geodesic) and Sandakan to Tawau (391.07 km / 216.41 km geodesic) — summing to 661.4 km, matching the sheet's 662 km almost exactly and confirming the corridor bends north to Sandakan before continuing south to Tawau. Recommend a routes-repo follow-up: redraw P1067 as a two-leg corridor via Sandakan (RouteAccuracy can stay 'low' — this is still a schematic corridor, not a precision alignment) rather than replacing the direct line; update RouteNotes from 'not found' to note the Sandakan waypoint. No sheet cell changes beyond adding the LengthKnown ref below.
resolutions.researcher_notes: Three independent sources all state the TSGP as a 662 km pipeline running from Kimanis Gas Terminal (west coast) to Sandakan and Tawau (east coast), consistent with the sheet's LengthKnownKm=662: (1) Sinar Project / Politikus procurement tracker (Malaysian civil-society open-data project, independent of any wire story) — 'building a 662km gas pipeline from the Kimanis Gas Terminal on Sabah's west coast to Sandakan and Tawau on Sabah's east coast'; (2) AidData (William & Mary research lab, China Eximbank loan-tracking project record) — 'The TSGP involves the construction of a 662 km gas pipeline from Kimanis Gas Terminal facilities to gas turbine power generation plants in Sandakan, Lahad Datu and Tawau'; (3) Malaysiakini (Malaysian news outlet) — 'The TSGP project involved building a 662km gas pipeline from Kimanis Gas Terminal to Sandakan and Tawau'. All three name Sandakan as an explicit waypoint (AidData adds Lahad Datu), which is materially north of a direct Kimanis-Tawau line — this is why the true route is longer than the ~380 km great-circle-ish distance GEM's drawn LineString spans. Could NOT find a source giving an explicit two-segment km breakdown in independent citable press/NGO/research coverage; the 270/391 km segment split comes only from the GulfPub PE World Map scrape already staged in this batch's recon-gulfpub-20260812/match_diff.json (overlaps[2] and overlaps[3], oid 101411 and 101412 — Tier-2, not usable as a [ref], but its geometry corroborates the Sandakan-detour shape and its segment lengths sum to 661.4 km, within rounding of the sheet's 662). Daily Express Malaysia's dedicated 'Issues concerning the Trans Sabah Gas Pipeline Project' piece (a natural primary source, discussed the PAC/1MDB-era cost detail) returned HTTP 403 and could not be read or verified — noted as unverifiable, not cited. Did not find a Suria Strategic Energy Resources corporate statement with a length figure (would bear on the separately-flagged Owner1/CPPB-vs-Suria question, not restated here per instructions). Conclusion: 662 km is correct; the route geometry is under-drawn, not the length value.
